CFP parcels with major canopy loss

Houghton & Keweenaw Counties, Michigan

Author

Randy Swaty

Published

September 17, 2026

Summary

Using Commercial Forest Parcel (CFP) data for 2020 and 2026 from the Michigan Department of Natural Resources alongside the USFS FIA Total Canopy Cover (TCC) dataset, I looked for parcels that had a canopy cover change > 20% between 2020 and 2026. All of the information below is for parcels that had the largest change in canopy cover.

Of 2128 CFP parcels ≥20 acres, 72 parcels (~1.2219^{4} acres) lost more than 20 percentage points of mean tree canopy from 2020 to 2025. Almost all stayed Forest Industry by owner type — but most changed legal name, led by TRG Threshold → Verdant Timber.

Takeaway

The ~12k acres of major canopy loss are concentrated on forest-industry CFP land that kept the forest industry type label. Continuity of owner type masks substantial legal-name turnover, especially TRG Threshold Timber → Verdant Timber (~55 parcels / ~9,900 ac) and Keweenaw Land Association → Sage Timber (8 parcels / ~600 ac). None of these 72 parcels left the CFP between 2020 and 2026.

Methods (short)

  • Unit: 2020 CFP parcels with attribute acres ≥ 20 (parid).
  • Canopy: zonal mean USFS/NLCD TCC on the 30 m grid, 2020 vs 2025 (latest annual TCC; ownership snapshot is 2026).
  • Major loss: mean ΔTCC < −20 percentage points (72 of 2,128 ranked parcels).
  • Ownership: 2020 owner_type / search_nam; 2026 OwnerTypeT / FullLegalN, joined on parid.
  • Name match: loose string compare (case, punctuation, LLC/Inc stripped). Source table: data/processed/cfp_parcel_tcc_change_by_owner_type.csv (scripts/09_cfp_parcel_tcc_change.R).
